title: CoT Unfaithfulness + Monitoring Failure: When Safety Watchers Are Blind

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The core finding that CoT monitoring is fragile and fails at non-trivial rates for problematic behavior has been established by OpenAI, Anthropic, METR, and Frontier Model Forum in 2025. The nuanced answer (complexity-dependent monitorability) is already documented.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires identifying both problematic model behavior and unfaithful CoT in the same outputs. Need a way to assess whether CoT reflects actual reasoning. Methodologically demanding but existing frameworks (hint injection, Petri) provide templates. Feasible with mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two-dimensional measurement (problematic behavior + unfaithful CoT) plus characterization of which behavior types produce unfaithful cover. Moderate scope. Could be narrowed to a specific behavior type for a 30-hour project.

novelty.reasoning: This is one of the most actively studied topics in AI safety in 2025. OpenAI's 'Evaluating chain-of-thought monitorability' directly measures monitoring failure from CoT unfaithfulness. 'Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety' (arxiv 2507.11473) frames exactly this problem. METR's work shows CoT may be informative despite unfaithfulness. 'When Chain of Thought is Necessary, Language Models Struggle to Evade Monitors' (arxiv 2507.05246) tests the complexity-dependent nature of monitoring evasion. Multiple papers measure bypass rates (16-36%), phase transitions in monitorability, and faithfulness rates across frontier models. The core question (does CoT monitoring fail when behavior is problematic?) has been extensively studied with nuanced answers.
